name: heaptrack
workload: Heap allocation profiling of real-world applications via LD_PRELOAD interposition of malloc and friends.
claimed_speedup: README: overhead in time and memory is 'significantly lower' than massif; multi-threaded programs are not serialized; CPU-bound code is not slowed down. No numbers.
license: LGPL-2.1-or-later (REUSE LICENSES folder; exact SPDX expression not confirmed)
tradeoffs: Only sees malloc-family calls; pool allocators need annotation; massif can profile page allocations and stacks.
caveats: Qualitative claim only, no numbers. HN thread comments (snippets) also say heaptrack handles millions of allocations per second. Exact license expression not verified.
found_via: Hacker News: search 'Show HN memory profiler heaptrack faster than massif valgrind' (threads comparing heaptrack and massif/bytehound)

name: bytehound
workload: Memory profiling of native programs (C/C++ via LD_PRELOAD) recording every allocation with full stack traces.
claimed_speedup: README: custom stack unwinding makes it 'a lot cheaper than other similar tools, potentially up to orders of magnitude faster in some cases'. No numbers.
tradeoffs: Linux only; preload library written in Rust (nightly toolchain to build); no support for profiling by sampling.
caveats: No numbers or named baseline in the README; the heaptrack and Valgrind comparison comes from the author's HN comments (seen only as search snippets, thread not openable). Last commit about 3 years old.
found_via: Hacker News: 'Show HN: I wrote a tool in Rust for tracking all allocations in a Linux process' and comment thread comparing it with heaptrack

name: Dr. Memory
workload: Memory error checking (uninitialized reads, unaddressable accesses, leaks) on SPEC CPU2006 under Linux.
claimed_speedup: README: 'faster than comparable tools, including Valgrind', shown as a chart in the CGO 2011 paper; Valgrind cannot run 434.zeusmp and 447.dealII. No numbers on the page.
tradeoffs: Memory checker rather than profiler; built on DynamoRIO; paper results are from 2011 on SPEC2006.
caveats: Paper (burningcutlery.com) is on a blocked host, so numbers were not read; tier B rests on the peer-reviewed CGO 2011 paper cited by the README. Old comparison against an old Valgrind version. Category fit is loose (memory checker).
found_via: Hacker News: 'Dr. Memory: A Memory Checker Faster Than Valgrind' (search 'Show HN low overhead profiler faster than Valgrind')

name: Perforator
workload: Fleet-wide eBPF CPU profiling of C++, C, Go and Rust services, unwinding without frame pointers or host debug symbols.
claimed_speedup: README: collects CPU profiles from production 'without affecting its performance'; agent uses 512Mb RAM and <1% of host CPUs. No comparison against perf with numbers.
license: Apache-2.0 (eBPF unwinder and JVM parts GPL-2.0)
stars_or_usage: 3.4k stars; deployed on tens of thousands of Yandex servers
tradeoffs: x86-64 Linux, needs a cluster-style deployment for full use; mostly Go with C eBPF code.
caveats: Overhead figure is a first-party resource cap, not a measured speedup over perf; baseline is inferred. The Medium and Habr posts are blocked. Last commit date not read. eBPF code is GPL-2.0.
found_via: Hacker News: 'Show HN: Perforator' (search 'Show HN profiler eBPF continuous profiling overhead perf comparison')

name: bpftime
workload: Userspace eBPF runtime that runs uprobe and syscall-hook programs in the target process instead of trapping into the kernel.
claimed_speedup: README: 'up to a 10x speedup in Uprobe overhead compared to kernel uprobe and uretprobe, up to a 10x faster than NVbit'
tradeoffs: Userspace runtime with LD_PRELOAD or injection; not all kernel eBPF helpers and maps are available; adds its own runtime and shared-memory maps.
caveats: Linked benchmark repo (eunomia-bpf/bpf-benchmark) now describes an unrelated LLM eBPF-optimization benchmark and holds no uprobe numbers on its front page, so the claim is README-only. Baseline is kernel uprobes, not perf, gprof or Valgrind. Numbers 'up to'.
found_via: Hacker News: 'Bpftime: Userspace eBPF runtime for fast Uprobe and Syscall hook and Plugins' (search 'Show HN tracing function calls uftrace low overhead gprof alternative')
